_meta.purpose: The closed band vocabulary seed-contract.md §3 requires: authors write powerBand / costBand / dropBand / variance, never a magnitude, weight, probability, or quantity. This file is what makes each band resolve to a real number, and it is the only place that resolution logic lives. Consumed by ~125 parallel authoring agents and by every generator that expands a seed file into rows.
_meta.immutability: FROZEN v1 once an owner flips `frozen` to true and authoring begins against it. Band enum members, their tier/step mapping, and every ratio/width constant below are never renumbered, rescaled, or reused for a different meaning after that point. A change to any number in this file after freeze is v2, minted only after an explicit owner re-run decision — never an in-place edit.
_meta.appendOnlyRule: Band enums are CLOSED, not append-only in the rarity-ladder sense. Every generator, lint, and downstream tier-bands artefact hardcodes the band list and its resolution formula; adding a band changes how every existing per-family `share` is interpreted (a new rung between `medium` and `high` shifts what `high` has always meant). Adding a band is therefore a reviewed, versioned change against this document, not a free append.
_meta.idGrammarNote: Band values are bare lowercase words, no punctuation, no dots, no digits — they are content values inside a seed field (`powerBand: "medium"`), never part of an id grammar.

unitsCorrectionLedger.whatWasWrong: definitions.md §2 (and atom-family-library.md §2a's worked example) stated every derived-channel magnitude is sigmoid resolver points at scale 100.0. Verified against code, that is true only for accuracy/dodge/crit — combat.power.*, combat.defense.* and combat.shield.* are flat game units: CombatProbabilityPolicy declares no PowerScale/DefenseScale (src/FusionRpg.Core/Stats/Derived/CombatPolicies.cs:9-14), and (power − defense) is summed straight into the damage term (src/FusionRpg.Core/Combat/OverlayCombatCalculator.cs:84-89,104; CombatDerivedReader.cs:9-10).
unitsCorrectionLedger.consequence: six of the twelve stat.derived families move from this file's sigmoidDerivedChannel group to its flatDerivedChannel group: elemental_power, elemental_defense, shield_capacity, shield_toughness, shield_pen, shield_regen.
unitsCorrectionLedger.whatThisMeansForSsotAffixes: ssot-affixes.md §4.5's ONLY numeric worked example for a stat.derived family is `elemental_power`, and it was computed against the sigmoid calibration anchor (the 150-point crit-hunter trait). That table does NOT survive the correction for `elemental_power` itself — a combat.power.* family needs a game-units share against a base-damage curve, which does not exist yet (blocked on E12 / a `B_family` for combat.power, per atom-family-library.md §3.2's stat.derived quarantine). The ARITHMETIC in that table is still valid sigmoid arithmetic; this registry reassigns it, relabelled, as the sigmoidDerivedChannel worked example below, because a genuinely sigmoid family (precision, keen_edge, ...) has none of its own yet.

powerBand.description: What an author writes instead of a magnitude, a ratio, a chance, or a duration on any atom-bearing content (affixes, implicits, milestone atoms, unique fixed cores).
powerBand.bandCountRationale: 5, one per tier the atom layer already has. `atom_id` derives as `{family_id}[.{variant}].t{tier}` for exactly five tiers (definitions.md §1); ssot-affixes.md's item-level gating (§4.6) and tier-weight curve (§4.8) are both authored against exactly five rungs. A sixth powerBand would need a sixth `.t6` atom row on every family — an atom-layer change, not a bands-registry one. Fewer would waste tiers the schema already reserves and already prices.

tierScaling.description: The ratio between tiers and the default band width, shared by every channel-family group below unless a family's own tier-bands input overrides it (ssot-affixes.md §5.4 — out of this registry's scope).
tierScaling.magnitudeRatioNote: r = 1.75, the default tier-to-tier midpoint ratio for a value or chance ladder. t1 → t5 spans ~9.4x.
tierScaling.durationRatioNote: r = 1.4, MANDATORY (not a default) for the duration half of any status.apply family's two-ladder. Duration stacks across sources and the roster; magnitude/chance does not. ssot-affixes.md §4.5: 'control families ladder duration at r=1.4, never at 1.75' — a five-tier duration ladder at 1.75 would put tier-5 control at ~7.5s and let three items chain a permanent lock.
tierScaling.bandWidthNote: ±33% around each tier's midpoint (lo_t = round_legible(0.67 × m_t), hi_t = round_legible(1.33 × m_t)). This is powerBand's own default width and is exactly what `variance: "normal"` reproduces below.
tierScaling.roundLegible: every m_1, m_t, lo_t, hi_t snaps to a human number (1 / 2 / 5 significance) without breaking the overlap invariant below; a snap that breaks it is rejected at import (ssot-affixes.md §4.5).

overlap.requirement: hi_t must be >= lo_(t+1) for every adjacent tier pair — the rarity ladder's overlap guarantee (OD4) depends on it, and it must hold by construction, not by luck on any one family's numbers.

magnitudeProof.conclusion: 1985 > 1750, so hi_t (1.33 × m_t) is always >= lo_(t+1) (0.67 × 1.75 × m_t = 1.1725 × m_t) for the default magnitude ratio. Overlap holds for every family that uses the default width and ratio.

durationProof.conclusion: 1985 > 1400 by a wider margin than the magnitude case — duration's flatter ratio overlaps even more comfortably.

knownEdgeCase.issue: m1 resolves to 4 game units (below the 5-unit legibility floor), so hi_1 = 5 and lo_2 = 5 are EQUAL rather than strictly overlapping — the invariant holds only as a tie.
knownEdgeCase.resolution: not relaxed here. A family whose m1 < 5 game units trips the legibility lint; the documented fix is to let that family's Increased sibling (e.g. ferocity for might) carry the fine grain, never to introduce a fractional unit.

channelFamilyGroups.description: A powerBand carries no unit. The channel family it is attached to decides the unit and the formula — this is the four-way split the whole file exists to make explicit.

primaryChannel.unit: op-dependent: Flat -> game units (hit points, attack points, or an interval channel's own unit); Increased or More -> integer per-mille (a ratio against the identity 1000‰); an interval channel (quickening/flourishing/swiftness) -> integer ms, Flat-shaped
primaryChannel.formula: m1 = round_legible(sharePermille × referenceBaseGameUnits(referenceLevel) / 1000); m_t = round_legible(m1 × ratioPerMille^(t-1) / 1000^(t-1)); lo_t = round_legible(bandFloorPerMille × m_t / 1000); hi_t = round_legible(bandCeilingPerMille × m_t / 1000)
primaryChannel.sharePermilleOwnership: sharePermille is authored per primary channel in a SEPARATE generator-input artefact (ssot-affixes.md §5.4's 'tier-bands', owned by I8, not yet built). This registry fixes the method and cites the two committed worked examples below; it supplies no sharePermille for any channel not shown. A generator with no authored share for a channel must reject at import, not guess one.

workedExamples.status: illustrative, inherited, not balanced — reproduced here for calibration, not re-derived

workedExamples.note: m1 = 4, below the 5-unit legibility floor — see tierScaling.overlap.knownEdgeCase. Kept as-is deliberately; the fix lives on `ferocity`, not here.

referenceBase.source: identity ratio (no base curve for a ratio family)

workedExamples.note: sharePermille=16 legibilises to a tier-1 midpoint of 15‰, not 16‰ — the round_legible snap, reproduced exactly from source.

flatDerivedChannel.unit: op-dependent: Flat -> game units (additive damage, or hit-point-equivalent shield absorb) — same formula shape as primaryChannel; Increased -> integer per-mille; Replace/Flag carry no tier-band magnitude at all and are out of powerBand's scope (structural, not scaled)
flatDerivedChannel.memberFamiliesSource: atom-family-library.md §3.2, RECLASSIFIED here per the units correction (_meta.unitsCorrectionLedger) — these six were the ones definitions.md §2 mis-stated as sigmoid.
flatDerivedChannel.formula: identical shape to primaryChannel.formula: m1 = round_legible(sharePermille × referenceBaseGameUnits(referenceLevel) / 1000), then the same tier ladder and band width.
flatDerivedChannel.note: No worked example survives for this group. ssot-affixes.md §4.5's only stat.derived numeric table (`elemental_power`) was computed against the SIGMOID calibration anchor and belongs, arithmetically, to sigmoidDerivedChannel below — it cannot be reused here without a real `B_family` base-damage/defense curve, which does not exist yet. All six families in this group are additionally quarantined at runtime (`stat.derived` is None/None/None until E12, atom-family-library.md §3.2) — content authored against them mints rows nothing can bind until then. Author against this group only for a wave that already accepts pending content; do not invent a sharePermille here.

sigmoidDerivedChannel.unit: resolver points (sigmoid scale) — Flat-shaped magnitude only. AccuracyScale = CritRateScale = CritDamageScale = 100.0 (src/FusionRpg.Core/Stats/Derived/CombatPolicies.cs:9-12), so 100 points is one full sigmoid unit.
sigmoidDerivedChannel.memberFamiliesSource: atom-family-library.md §3.2 — combat.accuracy.*, combat.dodge.*, combat.crit.rate.*, combat.crit.damage.*, combat.crit.resist.*, combat.crit.resist.damage.*. These six are the ones definitions.md's sigmoid claim was actually correct about.

calibrationAnchor.source: definitions.md §2 and atom-layer-handoff.md §1, both citing the same trait
calibrationAnchor.trait: critical-hunter grants +150 resolver points, moving crit rate from ~7.6% to ~26.9%
calibrationAnchor.rule: an affix must not outclass a named trait — tier 5 of a sigmoid family should top out near a third of 150 points, i.e. ~50 points.

sigmoidDerivedChannel.formula: same tier ladder and band width as primaryChannel/flatDerivedChannel, but the reference base is the calibration anchor above rather than a BattleRuleset curve: m1 = round_legible(sharePermille × 150 / 1000), scaled so tier 5 lands near the ~50-point target.

workedExamples.family: a sigmoid family (illustrative placeholder — e.g. precision or keen_edge)
workedExamples.sourceRef: ssot-affixes.md §4.5, REASSIGNED — this is the exact numeric table §4.5 authored under the name `elemental_power`. The arithmetic is genuine sigmoid-points arithmetic anchored to the 150-point calibration; only the family label was wrong (elemental_power is combat.power.*, corrected to flatDerivedChannel above). No worked example in the source corpus is currently authored under a correctly-named sigmoid family — this table is reused here, relabelled, precisely because none exists.

statusMagnitudeAndDuration.unit: integer per-mille for a status's applied power/resist magnitude and for a status.apply family's trigger chance; integer ms for a status.apply family's duration

memberFamilies.statusChannelExcludedNote: status.expose.* (family `susceptibility`) has zero readers today and is not authored at all until it has a consumer (atom-family-library.md §3.2). Do not author against it.

statusMagnitudeAndDuration.memberFamiliesSource: atom-family-library.md §3.2 (status-channel families) and §3.4 (the 20 status.apply families that actually exist — the library's own header count of 21 is a documented off-by-one, ssot-affixes.md §4.2)

twoLadderRule.statement: magnitude and trigger-chance ladders use tierScaling.magnitudeRatioPerMille (1750‰) by default; a status.apply family's DURATION ladder must use tierScaling.durationRatioPerMille (1400‰) — mandatory, not a family choice.

statusMagnitudeAndDuration.note: on-hit trigger-chance ladders on resource.delta riders (e.g. searing_strike's 200‰ -> 400‰ over five tiers, ssot-affixes.md §4.5) are a distinct, deliberately flatter, family-specific arithmetic — that shape is an explicit per-family override recorded in the family's own tier-bands input, never this registry's default. Do not apply the freezing example's chance ratio to an on-hit rider family.

familiesOutOfFourWaySplit.note: resource.delta, status.clear, shield.grant, spawn.entity, board.action, grid.*, box.set and resource.economy families (searing_strike, lifesteal, retribution, deathblast, regeneration, martyrdom, warded, summoner, gardener, volley, the four board-action families, gravemaking, gravedigging, terraforming, sunbloom, midas, cleansing) were never mis-specified as sigmoid by definitions.md §2 — they are not part of the units correction and are not one of this file's four named groups. A generator resolves their magnitude the same way as primaryChannel's Flat sub-case (game units) and, where a trigger chance exists, the same way as statusMagnitudeAndDuration's chance sub-case, by analogy — this registry does not define a fifth channelFamilyGroup for them.

costBand.description: What an author writes on a recipe, an operation (enhance/reroll/craft), or any other spend, instead of a souls count or a material quantity.
costBand.bandCountRationale: 5, to give the souls-only / no-shard operations shipped in ssot-materials-crafting.md §7.4 (socket-an-insert at 10 souls flat, forge-a-base's low souls-only tier) a rung below the first shard-gated one, while still landing 'steep' exactly on the reroll program's already-committed 4000‰ escalation ceiling (ssot-reroll.md §5.1) — so an author never has to guess whether their band exceeds what the engine itself treats as maximal.
costBand.resolvesTo: an integer per-mille multiplier applied, at GENERATION TIME (not at runtime), against a recipe's or operation's base cost — a souls count and/or a material qty — taken from I9's reference cost table (ssot-materials-crafting.md §7.4) or an operation's own base cost (ssot-enhancement.md §7.5, ssot-reroll.md §5.3). The generator emits the final integer quantity into the content row; nothing at runtime re-evaluates the band.

multiplierTable.note: below the baseline unit; for operations that are already deliberately near-free, e.g. socket-an-insert (ssot-materials-crafting.md §7.4: 10 souls and nothing else).
the baseline unit multiplier (x1.000) — an author who is unsure picks this.

deliberately equal to the reroll program's ESCALATION‰ hard ceiling (ssot-reroll.md §5.1: min(4000, 1000 + 250 × priorOps)) — 'steep' names the ceiling that mechanism already converges to, rather than inventing an unrelated number.

reserved for authored one-off sinks (e.g. an Imprint-shaped guarantee, ssot-reroll.md §3.4/§5.3, priced at ~10x a base Reforge) — not for anything that recurs per attempt, which is escalation's job, not costBand's.

application.roundingRule: always ceiling, integer — mirrors the shipped rule for `qty_curve_id` (ssot-materials-crafting.md §6.2: 'always ceiling, so no curve can ever make a cost free')

costBand.distinctFrom: the runtime `qty_curve_id` -> `effect_curve` mechanism (ssot-materials-crafting.md §6.2), which is restricted to `input: rarity` / `input: tier`, lives in the database, and is evaluated at spend time. costBand is resolved once, by the generator, before import — consistent with seed-contract.md §1's 'anything a formula can compute is not authored' rule: the band is authored, the multiplier table here is the formula, and the resulting integer is what gets checked in.
costBand.note: the 500/1000/2000/4000/8000 doubling ladder is invented for this registry with no formula source beyond anchoring 'steep' to the already-committed 4000‰ escalation ceiling. The doubling shape itself echoes the reroll program's own `ANCHOR_MULT = 2^K` (ssot-reroll.md §5.1) but is not derived from it — it is a fresh, independently-invented ladder.

dropBand.description: What an author writes on a single drop_table_entry row, or an affix family's W_family deviation, instead of a raw integer weight.
dropBand.bandCountRationale: 5, deliberately worded to share NO vocabulary with I1's rarity ladder — whose shipped rungs (core.v1.json: chaff/sprout/grafted/cultivated/fused/chimeric/heirloom/firstseed/sunwoven/almanac) and whose illustrative drop-table ordinals (ssot-generation.md §4.2: common/uncommon/rare/epic/mythic/relic/unique) both already use rarity-flavoured words for a DIFFERENT axis — an item's own rarity. dropBand names a ROW's pull within a table or pool, never an item's rarity, and reusing 'common'/'uncommon' here would tempt an author to type a rarity rung into a weight field.
dropBand.resolvesTo: a plain positive integer weight — never per-mille (ssot-generation.md §4.2: 'Weights are plain integers out of 100,000, not per-mille') — written at generation time into `drop_table_entry.weight` or into an `effect_container_pool` row's explicit `W_family` deviation (ssot-affixes.md §4.8).

distinctFrom.rarityLadder: I1's rarity rungs (core.v1.json `rarity.ladder`) name an ITEM'S rarity, drawn once per drop (ssot-generation.md §7). dropBand names one ROW's relative pull within a drop table or an affix pool and never appears on an item itself.
distinctFrom.tierWeight: the pool-row TIER weight (1000/600/300/120/35 for t1-t5, ~29:1 span) is DERIVED automatically from an atom's `tier`, never authored (ssot-affixes.md §4.8: 'W_family = 1, and this is a rule, not a default'). dropBand exists only for the axis that curve does not cover: drop_table_entry rows (equipment/material/currency/insert/charm/nothing, ssot-generation.md §5.3) and an explicit, reasoned `W_family` deviation.

dropBand.zeroWeight: weight = 0 (crafted-only, or a row kept but never drawn, ssot-materials-crafting.md / spec-container-schema.md) is authored directly as the schema's own explicit zero — a structural count, not a band — never via a dropBand value. A dropBand always resolves to a positive integer >= 1.
dropBand.note: the 1000/300/90/25/7 ladder (~3.3x per step) is invented for this registry with no formula source. It was sized to span roughly the same order of magnitude the shipped illustrative rarity-drop-weight ladder spans (ssot-generation.md §4.2: 41000 down to 300, ~137:1 top to bottom) while giving an author only five coarse, named steps instead of a raw weight to invent.

variance.description: What an author writes on one slot (typically a unique's fixed-core `varianceSlot`, seed-contract.md §10) to widen or narrow that slot's roll range away from powerBand's default band width.
variance.bandCountRationale: 3 — the coarsest vocabulary that still lets a slot diverge from the default width in either direction. This knob only ever nudges one already-resolved number (the ± width around a tier midpoint); a 5-step ladder would reproduce the exact over-precision problem seed-contract.md §3 exists to prevent, for an axis with far less design weight than powerBand's own tier.
variance.resolvesTo: a per-mille +/- width around a tier midpoint, REPLACING powerBand.tierScaling's default bandFloorPerMille / bandCeilingPerMille for the one slot it is authored on. It does not change the midpoint, the tier, or the unit — only how wide the roll range around that midpoint is.

widthTable.widthDescription: +/-330 permille (+/-33%) — identical to powerBand.tierScaling's default. A seed that omits `variance` entirely gets exactly this width; `variance: "normal"` is documentation, not a behaviour change.

variance.appliesTo: any resolved magnitude regardless of channelFamilyGroup — game units, resolver points, chance permille, or duration ms alike. variance is a pure width multiplier on whatever unit the group already resolved to, so it needs no group-specific case.
variance.overlapApplicability: the adjacent-tier overlap invariant (powerBand.tierScaling.overlap) is a POOL-AUTHORING rule: it applies only where a value is drawn across a rarity ladder's tier window (ssot-affixes.md §3.5). A unique's fixed-core `varianceSlot` (seed-contract.md §10) is never drawn from a tier window — it is a single authored roll — so narrowing it to `narrow` cannot violate that invariant; there is no adjacent tier for it to overlap with. Only a pool-authored family's own variance override (if one is ever authored) is checked against the invariant.
variance.note: the +/-15% / +/-33% / +/-50% ladder is invented for this registry, except +/-33% itself, which is NOT invented — it is powerBand.tierScaling's already-committed default (ssot-affixes.md §4.5). +/-15% and +/-50% have no source beyond being roughly half of, and one and a half times, that committed default.

frozenNote: FROZEN v1. Consumed by the wave-1 authoring fleet. No in-place edit from here: a required change is registryVersion 2 plus an explicit decision on which partitions re-run. A silently edited registry splits the corpus into pre-edit and post-edit semantics that nothing downstream can tell apart.
stage1aFrozen: Stage 1a authored and validated at 0 errors (205 entries, 25 files). From here a change to this registry invalidates authored content unless minCompatibleVersion says otherwise.
